title: the scheduler: the tools of one answer run together
intent: The registry accepts one tool call at a time, and the state machine has a single awaiting-tool state, so a task that needs five reads costs five turns of the model: five times the tokens, five times the context. The reference harnesses run the calls of one answer concurrently, with a concurrency mode declared per tool and a barrier at the end of the batch. This wave is that scheduler.
checks: ./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/test-yeah-state.el tests/unit/test-yeah-loop.el tests/unit/test-yeah-tools.el tests/unit/test-yeah-perm.el tests/unit/test-yeah-session.el tests/unit/test-yeah-compact.el tests/unit/test-yeah-undo.el tests/unit/test-yeah-acp.el tests/unit/test-yeah-emcp.el tests/unit/test-yeah-gptel.el tests/unit/test-yeah-subagent.el tests/unit/test-yeah-shell.el tests/unit/test-yeah-codes.el
objection: Parallel tools make the log order undefined, and a log whose order depends on which tool finished first is harder to read than a log that is merely slow.
refuted_by: Two calls of one batch that touch the same file and are serialised by a per-resource lock, while calls on different files overlap in time. If the order of the records cannot be reconstructed, the log is no longer a log.
